newsitem.title: ISRAEL: West Bank clashes during U.S. Mideast peace drive.
newsitem.headline: West Bank clashes during U.S. Mideast peace drive.

text.p: Stone-throwing Palestinians battled Israeli soldiers in the West Bank on Friday in clashes that underscored the hardships facing a U.S. Middle East peace-saving mission.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, in a move likely to anger Palestinians, reaffirmed its policy to strengthen Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Netanyahu, reporting on a peace mission by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, was quoted in a cabinet statement as having said efforts to revive talks stalled for nearly two months were still in an "exploratory" phase.

Clashes erupted in the West Bank town of Hebron on Friday when hundreds of Palestinian youths stoned Israeli soldiers along the invisible line that divides the city between Palestinian and Israeli rule.
Palestinian witnesses said Israeli soldiers firing rubber bullets wounded at least three Arabs. Palestinian police pushed the demonstrators back to stop the clashes.

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks have been stuck since the Jewish state began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The Palestinian Authority insists Israel suspend settlement activity before resuming peace talks.

The cabinet statement quoted Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai as defending the demolition of illegal shacks put up by settlers of Yitzhar in the West Bank this week but the statement voiced regret at the way it was handled.
The statement said: "The government is acting to strengthen settlement."
Ross met Mordechai on Friday and was due to see Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank town of Ramallah later in the day.
On Thursday, Ross acknowledged after three hours of talks with Arafat in Gaza that there were difficult problems to solve. He later met Netanyahu in Jerusalem.

Security officials from both sides met along with CIA officers at the U.S. Embassy in Tel Aviv but Netanyahu told his cabinet that security cooperation had not resumed. Israel wants the Palestinians to crack down on "terrorism".
Palestinian officials said Arafat told Ross he wanted Israel to stop settlement activity in Jerusalem and in the rest of the West Bank before he could agree to restarting peace talks.

Saeb Erekat, a top Palestinian negotiator, told Israel Radio that the U.S. envoy brought no new ideas. Erekat said Arafat gave Ross documents on Israeli settlement activities on land captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
"We told Ross: Examine this report. You will find that Netanyahu is negotiating through the bulldozers," Erekat told the radio.

Israel and Jordan said Netanyahu and King Hussein had met secretly at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba for several hours late on Thursday to begin patching up a water dispute and to try to salvage Middle East peacemaking.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting with Netanyahu on Tuesday because of disagreements over water supplies Israel promised Jordan under a 1994 peace treaty.
